title: Introduce cost-affinity and provenance hydration for onboarded models (changelog-schema-v2)
author: Aisha Patel
description: Context & goal: Add an automated hydration step to the model onboarding pipeline that populates a provenance ledger and an optional cost-affinity tagset for each model variant, and introduce changelog-schema-v2 which carries compact, machine-readable change snippets for release automation. Motivation: customers and internal consumers need concise provenance + cost hints attached to each onboarded model so downstream serving, billing estimates, and release notes can consume deterministic metadata without requiring manual edits. This PR wires the hydration step into the intake path, migrates latest onboarding manifests to changelog-schema-v2, and preserves a backward-compatible fallback for legacy manifests. Changes: 1) New hydration service (onboard/hydrator) that reads ingest manifests, computes provenance entries (source, commit, fingerprint, ingest-run-id) and derives cost-affinity hints (expected tokens/sec bucket, quantization-recommendation, likely GPU-families). 2) Changelog schema v2: introduces a small, typed "snippet" object for automated release blurb generation and links to the provenance ledger. 3) Migration script: tools/migrate_manifests_v2 which upgrades existing manifests in-place in a safe, idempotent way and writes a migration-log. 4) Integrations: console preview updated to show cost-affinity badges and a provenance timeline; registry API exposes /models/:id/provenance and /models/:id/affinity endpoints. 5) Tests & docs: unit tests for hydration logic, staging integration test with sample manifests, and docs/registry/onboard-provenance.md. Backwards compatibility & safety: hydration is enabled by default for new ingests but the intake pipeline accepts a feature flag to skip hydration for customers who manage their own metadata. Migration script writes a .backup and can be rolled back by revert-manifest.sh. Checklist: [x] unit tests added; [x] integration smoke in staging; [x] migration script included; [x] docs updated; [x] perf regression checked (<+2% latency at ingest). Rollout plan: stage in canary for 48 hours, monitor telemetry (ingest latency, migration error rate), then full deploy. Revert plan: disable hydration flag and roll back migration using backups (revert-manifest.sh). Related work: ENG-4572 (onboard observability), ENG-4620 (release automation).
commits: feat(onboard): add provenance hydrator pipeline; feat(schema): bump changelog to v2 and add snippet object; feat(api): add provenance + affinity endpoints; chore(migrate): add migrate_manifests_v2 and revert-manifest.sh; test: add hydrator unit and integration tests; docs: onboard-provenance.md and changelog-schema-v2.md
review_comments: Liam O'Connor: This looks good overall — two questions: (1) how expensive is the affinity computation at scale and (2) can we avoid storing duplicate provenance entries when manifests are re-submitted?

Aisha Patel: Affinity computation is O(n_layers) for the model header + a lightweight perf heuristic; we cache the affinity fingerprint per model-hash and the hydrator short-circuits if hash exists to avoid recompute. Dedup is handled by provenance ledger dedupe by ingest-run-id and model-hash (see hydrator.py lines ~120-160).
Marisol Chen: The migration script modifies manifests in-place — can we ensure atomicity? I want a dry-run mode and per-tenant failure isolation.

Aisha Patel: Added --dry-run and per-tenant commit logs; migration writes to <manifest>.backup and uses rename to make replacement atomic. See tools/migrate_manifests_v2.py commit. Also added alerting to onboard-migration-errors.yaml to catch partial failures.
Devon Brooks: CI flaked once on the staging smoke job; please confirm the rerun result and whether any test timing could be brittle.
Aisha Patel: The first CI failure was a 1s timing window in the staging test; increased test timeout and added retry for external mock. Rerun passed (CI job #7453).
testing: Unit tests: hydrator unit tests cover hash dedupe, affinity buckets, and provenance record format. Integration: staging smoke validates a sample manifest flow including migration and console preview. Perf: synthetic run of 10k manifests in staging cluster shows +1.8% median ingest latency and <5% peak memory increase. Migration: tested on a 2k-manifest snapshot; dry-run validated expected fields without mutating originals. CI: pipeline runs lint, unit, integration smoke, and staging-smoke; one flaky run rerun and passed.
release_notes: Added automatic provenance hydration during model onboard which records source, fingerprint, and ingest-run-id; introduced changelog-schema-v2 with compact snippet objects for automated release notes; attached cost-affinity hints to models to help serving routing and cost estimation. Migration tool included to upgrade existing manifests (dry-run supported).
rationale: This change reduces manual surface area for release notes and auditability while enabling cost-aware routing/serving decisions. The schema addition is intentionally small and typed so downstream consumers can incrementally adopt v2 snippets without full re-ingest. The hydration step is optional and guarded by flags to protect customers who manage metadata externally.
notes_for_sre: Watch onboard-migration-errors and onboarding-latency dashboards for the first 72 hours; perf telemetry added under registry.ingest.* and affinity.hydrator.*. We will run the migration during a controlled maintenance window; ensure backups for manifests/ storage are available.
